answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 15 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. The sable multiplier is published, charged in reef, and whisper lists each payment. A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 3430 identities would post 1226 proofs and burn roughly 62 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
